process_area.title: Program Strategy, Regulatory Setup & Partner Network

value_stream.name: Household Hazardous Waste, Paint & Used-Product Stewardship Take-Back Program

fields.Frequency: Annual strategy refresh; ad-hoc scope expansion
fields.Participants: VP Legal & Compliance, HSE Officer, Merchandising, Store Operations, Finance
fields.Trigger: Executive/ESG decision to launch a structured customer take-back program

workflows.name: Product Stewardship & Take-Back Program Strategy, Scope & Regulatory Mapping

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-map take-back streams to the active assortment so the scope stays current as SKUs change.
Controls: - CTL-791 (ensure controlled execution — Program Strategy, Regulatory Setup & Partner Network (PA-187.1).)
- operational: regulatory compliance scope; program budget adherence; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-22 (compliance), VS-179 (EPR/plastic), VS-152 (CSR)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: accepting streams BuildRight is not permitted/ equipped to handle (e.g. medical waste) creates regulatory and safety exposure; mitigated by an explicit scope list tied to the assortment and DENR-EMB permits.

- **Business-case risk**: a program run purely as cost without recovery revenue or footfall/ESG value is defunded; mitigated by quantifying recovery revenue (W5362) and ESG/CSR value in the business case.
System Touchpoints: - ESG/sustainability program module (VS-25); product-assortment cross-reference (VS-01); compliance mapping (VS-22).
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks elapsed per annual refresh; ~100 person-hours.

steps.activity: Define the take-back scope by stream (paint, used oil, batteries, lamps, pesticides/solvents, e-waste, cylinders) and map each to the product assortment BuildRight sells.

Map each stream to its regulatory regime: RA 6969 (Toxic Substances), RA 8749 (Clean Air), RA 9275 (Clean Water), RA 9003 (solid waste), RA 6969 hazardous-waste rules, DENR-EMB DAOs, and RA 11898 EPR where overlapping.
Set diversion targets, program KPIs, and the business case (footfall lift, ESG/CSR value, recovery revenue, cost of compliance).
Define phasing (pilot stores → regional → national) and the stream rollout sequence.
Approve the strategy at the ESG/steering committee and board ESG reporting (links VS-25/VS-36).

fields.Frequency: Initial registration per store/entity; periodic renewal (per DENR-EMB cycle)
fields.Participants: DENR-EMB liaison, HSE Officer, Facilities, Permit Portfolio (VS-166)
fields.Trigger: Program launch (W5345); new store added to the program; permit renewal
fields.Volume: ~200 store-level hazardous-waste generator registrations; ~5 entity-level permits

workflows.name: DENR-EMB Hazardous Waste Generator/Treater Registration & Permitting (RA 6969)

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-expiry alerts auto-gate per-store take-back; renewal applications pre-filled from the store profile.
Controls: - CTL-41: DENR/agency regulatory compliance; CTL-34 (permit-validity availability gate).
Cross-references: - links to VS-166 (permit portfolio), VS-24 (HSE), VS-22 (compliance), VS-76 (LGU)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Operating-without-permit risk**: accepting hazardous waste at a store that lacks DENR-EMB generator registration is itself a violation (RA 6969 penalties, store closure order); mitigated by gating take-back availability on a valid permit per store.
- **Permit-lapse risk**: an expired generator registration unnoticed takes the whole store's take-back offline; mitigated by 60–90-day renewal alerts in the permit portfolio.
System Touchpoints: - Permit/portfolio register (VS-166) with DENR-EMB expiry alerts; hazardous-waste ledger module; availability gate on permit validity.
Time Estimate: - ~6–12 weeks elapsed initial; ~2–4 person-hours per renewal.

steps.activity: Register each participating store as a hazardous-waste generator with DENR-EMB (RA 6969 / DAO permits) for the streams it will accept.
Secure the entity-level permits (generator, and transporter/treater arrangements via accredited TSD — W5347).
Establish the per-store hazardous-waste storage area/containment to DENR spec (links W5349).
Record permits in the license/permit portfolio with renewal alerts (VS-166); gate take-back availability on valid permit.
Maintain the required hazardous-waste register/ledger and reporting workflow (W5364).

fields.Participants: Compliance Specialist, HSE Officer, TPRM (VS-161), Finance

workflows.name: Take-Back Partner, Transporter & TSD (Treatment-Storage-Disposal) Facility Accreditation

Automation Opportunity: - DENR-accreditation status re-checked automatically from the DENR registry at each re-qualification cycle.
Controls: - CTL-06: vendor/TSD onboarding with DENR check; CTL-41 (regulatory partner compliance).
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (vendor mgmt), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-179 (EPR/PRO partners)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unaccredited-partner risk**: handing waste to a transporter/TSD whose DENR accreditation lapsed shifts liability for the waste back to BuildRight (cradle-to-grave under RA 6969); mitigated by accreditation verification at qualification and periodic re-check, and manifest cradle-to-grave tracking (W5351).
- **Concentration risk**: a single TSD failure halts a stream's disposal and stockpiles hazardous waste at stores; mitigated by at least two accredited partners per major stream per region.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master (VS-03) flagged "DENR-accredited TSD"; TPRM inventory (VS-161); manifest/chain-of-custody link (W5351).
Time Estimate: - ~6–8 weeks elapsed initial; ~1 week per periodic re-qualification.

steps.activity: Identify DENR-accredited hazardous-waste transporters and TSD facilities per stream (paint recycler, oil re-refiner, battery recycler, lamp/hg handler, e-waste processor).
Qualify each on DENR accreditation, capacity, coverage, pricing, and HSSE record (TPRM — VS-161).
Negotiate service agreements with manifest/handling fees, SLAs, and reporting obligations.
Record partners in the vendor/TSD master; link to the manifest chain-of-custody (W5351).
Monitor partner performance, accreditation validity, and incidents (W5365); re-qualify periodically.

fields.Frequency: Annual agreement cycle; per new brand scheme
fields.Trigger: Program setup; brand EPR/stewardship scheme participation

workflows.name: Manufacturer/Brand Stewardship Partnership, Co-Funding & EPR Alignment

Automation Opportunity: - Co-funding auto-reconciled against scanned returns by brand/SKU.
Controls: - CTL-39: vendor rebate/co-funding accuracy; CTL-34 (ESG claim substantiation).
Cross-references: - links to VS-39 (vendor rebates), VS-179 (EPR), VS-25 (ESG reporting), VS-14 (marketing claims)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Greenwashing risk**: claiming a brand-funded take-back the brand does not actually fund/report; mitigated by co-funding reconciliation against actual returns and audited ESG reporting.
- **Double-funding risk**: counting the same recovery against both BuildRight's plastic EPR (VS-179) and a brand scheme; mitigated by explicit scope allocation between programs.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor/brand agreement module (VS-03); EPR/PRO coordination (VS-179); ESG reporting (VS-25); co-funding reconciliation (VS-39/W5367).
Time Estimate: - ~6–10 weeks elapsed per annual cycle; ~2 person-hours/week ongoing reconciliation.

steps.activity: Identify brands with existing stewardship schemes (paint brands, battery brands, lamp brands, electronics OEMs) that fund take-back.
Negotiate co-funding/subvention per unit returned and data-sharing for their stewardship reporting.
Align with the plastic-EPR program (VS-179) to avoid double-counting and consolidate PRO coordination.
Record co-funding terms and reconcile against actual returns (W5367).
Incorporate the program into BuildRight's ESG reporting and brand-sustainability claims (VS-25/VS-14).

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, BFP Fire Safety Inspector, Store Manager
fields.Trigger: New store added to the program (W5345/W5346)

workflows.name: In-Store Take-Back Collection Point Design, Containment & Safety Infrastructure

Automation Opportunity: - Standard collection-point design template and BOM auto-generated per stream set and store tier.
Controls: - CTL-171: take-back containment & asset safeguarding; operational: BFP/DENR commissioning gate.
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (facilities), VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG containment), VS-166 (BFP FSIC permits)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire/explosion risk**: a lithium-battery or solvent fire from improper containment in a retail store is catastrophic (BFP Fire Code, life safety); mitigated by fire-separated, stream-rated containment and BFP FSIC commissioning.
- **Customer-exposure risk**: leaking/fuming hazardous waste in customer-accessible area causes exposure complaints; mitigated by separated, ventilated containment outside customer flow.
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/CAPEX project module; BFP FSIC and DENR containment records; availability gate on commissioning.
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks elapsed per store; capital ~PHP 150k–500k per point.

steps.activity: Design the collection point: ventilated/curtained area, separated from stock and customer flow, with spill containment.
Install stream-specific containment: flame cabinets (paint/solvent), acid/lithium-rated bins with fire separation (batteries), mercury-tight containers (lamps), oil-rated bunded drums (used oil).
Equip with spill kits, PPE, fire suppression rated to the streams (BFP Fire Code FSIC), and emergency eyewash.
Signage, customer instructions, and max-quantity limits (W5350); staff training on handling.
Commission with HSE + BFP sign-off before first acceptance; gate acceptance on passed commissioning.

workflows.name: Take-Back Acceptance Policy, Eligibility, Quantity Limits & Customer Incentive Program

Automation Opportunity: - Online eligibility checker and appointment booking; loyalty points auto-issued on a validated acceptance scan.
Controls: - CTL-32: loyalty-points integrity on take-back incentives; CTL-46 (incentive-gaming fraud detection).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-acceptance risk**: accepting commercial-scale volumes under a residential policy turns the store into an unpermitted commercial hazardous-waste site; mitigated by quantity limits and a documented refusal script.
- **Incentive-abuse risk**: customers gaming a points-for-waste incentive (returning water-filled containers); mitigated by inspection at acceptance and per-customer/per-period caps.
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty/promotions engines (VS-13/VS-58) for incentive issuance; take-back transaction record per customer.
Time Estimate: - ~3 weeks per annual refresh; ~3 min per acceptance transaction at the counter.

steps.activity: Define eligibility (residential vs. commercial), acceptable condition, and per-visit/per-stream quantity limits per DENR-EMB small-quantity-generator rules.
Define refusal conditions (unidentified/unlabeled containers, commercial-scale volumes, excluded streams) and the staff script.
Design the customer incentive (loyalty points, discount coupon, or "drop a quart, get a brush" — links VS-58/VS-13).
Publish the policy in-store, online (W5352), and to staff; train counter staff on acceptance/refusal.
Monitor acceptance denials and customer complaints to tune the policy.

fields.Frequency: Per pickup batch; system maintained ongoing
fields.Participants: HSE Officer, TSD Transporter, Store Staff

workflows.name: Hazardous Waste Manifest, Transporter Accreditation & Chain-of-Custody System Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Manifest auto-generated from the weighed/counted store ledger; TSD-receipt confirmation auto-reconciles and flags gaps.
Controls: - CTL-791 (ensure controlled execution — Program Strategy, Regulatory Setup & Partner Network (PA-187.1).)
- operational: hazardous-waste manifest/DENR compliance; manifest quantity accuracy; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-114 (DG transport manifest), VS-161 (TPRM transporter), VS-88 (records retention of manifests)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cradle-to-grave liability risk**: a manifest gap (waste leaves the store but isn't confirmed at TSD) leaves BuildRight liable for the waste indefinitely under RA 6969; mitigated by mandatory TSD-receipt confirmation and discrepancy investigation.
- **Manifest-error risk**: an inaccurate manifest (wrong stream/quantity) is itself a DENR-EMB violation; mitigated by manifest auto-generated from the weighed/counted ledger rather than hand-keyed.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste manifest/chain-of-custody module; DENR-EMB format; TSD transporter accreditation link (W5347); store hazardous-waste ledger.
Time Estimate: - ~30–60 min per pickup batch at store; ongoing reconciliation.

steps.activity: Configure the hazardous-waste manifest module per DENR-EMB format (generator, transporter, TSD, stream, quantity, date).
At each pickup, generate the manifest from the store's hazardous-waste ledger (per-stream accumulation since last pickup).
Capture transporter accreditation, signature, and timestamp; hand over with spill-response acknowledgment.
Track the movement to TSD receipt and processing confirmation (cradle-to-grave).
Reconcile manifest-out vs. TSD-received; investigate any quantity discrepancy.

workflows.name: Take-Back Program Digital Platform, Customer Lookup & Awareness Campaign

Automation Opportunity: - Lookup auto-pulled from the live per-store stream/permit matrix; campaign analytics auto-fed.
Controls: - CTL-27: customer data on lookups/bookings; operational: lookup gated by live per-store permit validity.
Cross-references: - links to VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-75 (app), VS-14 (marketing), VS-137 (PIM), VS-152 (CSR)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-direction risk**: a customer told online that a stream is accepted at a store that isn't yet permitted (W5346) causes a refused-load complaint; mitigated by lookup driven by the live per-store permit/availability gate.
- **Low-awareness risk**: a program no one knows about underperforms; mitigated by campaign cycles tied to seasonal cleanout peaks.
System Touchpoints: - Web/app lookup (VS-10/VS-75) on the take-back catalog; appointment/queue booking; campaign/analytics (VS-14/VS-28).
Time Estimate: - ~5 weeks initial platform; ~2 person-hours/week ongoing campaign.

steps.activity: Build a "what can I recycle where" lookup on web/app: stream → accepted at store X → quantity limits → incentive.
Integrate take-back appointment/queue booking for busy stores to avoid queueing with hazardous loads.
Run awareness campaigns (in-store, social, community/CSR — VS-152) tied to paint/seasonal cleanout peaks.
Provide in-store signage and staff talking points; train staff (VS-124).
Measure campaign reach, lookup-to-visit conversion, and participation lift (W5368).
